text.p: The Belgian unit of U.S. earth moving equipment maker Caterpillar is sacking 227, mainly young, blue-collar workers and cutting planned investment for 1997 by 20 percent to achieve necessary economies.

Union sources said management told the works council there would be unspecified cuts in investment planned for after 1997, while new, reduced pay, contracts would be offered to new staff hired from January 1, 1997.
Existing contracts would not be changed.

The company, which has been in an extended struggle with unions to introduce a five-year 1.8 billion franc cost cutting plan, said it would re-assess whether to continue what it called non-competitive jobs in Belgium or relocalise them.
The plan aimed at boosting competitiveness includes savings of 300 million francs on wages.
In an initial reaction Caterpillar unions called a strike for Thursday and Friday.
Earlier this month staff rejected the cost-cutting plan in a referendum. At the time management threatened tough measures.
"The economies must be realised...we were forced to take other measures," the sources quoted management as saying.
Caterpillar staff have been on strike for over 45 days and three attempts at arbitration have failed. The plant currently employs some 2,500 blue-collar workers and 1,000 white-collar staff.
